The text below is retained for historical reference and is NOT current law.\n\n166A. Public servant disobeying direction under law.\u2014Whoever, being a public servant,\u2014\n(a) knowingly disobeys any direction of the law which prohibits him from requiring the attendance at any place of any person for the purpose of investigation into an offence or any other matter, or\n(b) knowingly disobeys, to the prejudice of any person, any other direction of the law regulating the manner in which he shall conduct such investigation, or\n(c) fails to record any information given to him under sub-section (1) of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in relation to cognizable offence punishable u...nd is NOT current law.", "judicial_flag": null, "no_current_text": false}Answer:
This old section punished public servants who knowingly disobey legal directions during investigations or refuse to record certain complaints. It has been replaced by a new law since 1 July 2024.

What you can do:
- If a police officer refuses to file your complaint about a serious crime, remind them that recording it is their duty under the new criminal code.
- If they still refuse, you can send a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police or file it directly with a Magistrate.
- For police misconduct during investigation, you can file a complaint with the State Human Rights Commission or approach the District Magistrate.
- Keep copies of all written complaints and dates when you approached the police station.
- If this involves an old case from before July 2024, consult an advocate about which law version applies to your situation.

The successor law is found in the law. For offenses committed or investigations started after 1 July 2024, the new code applies instead of this section.

⚠️ Legal information, not legal advice. Consult an advocate. © Callistus Moses · MSafe Solutions.'
